newsitem.title: USA: Allegheny Power, DQE to merge.
newsitem.headline: Allegheny Power, DQE to merge.

text.p: Allegheny Power Systems Inc and DQE Inc, the parent of Duquesne Light Co, said Monday they had agreed to a stock-swap merger that would create a company with a market capitalization of $10.6 billion.
They said their boards had unanimously approved a definitive merger agreement.
The combined company will be called Allegheny Energy, they said.
The merger will be accounted for as a pooling of interests and is expected to be accretive to earnings in the first year after the close of the deal, they said.
Under the agreement, DQE shareholders will receive 1.12 shares of Allegheny Power for each of their DQE shares.
In the merger, Allegheny Power will issue about 86.5 million shares valued at about $2.6 billion, based on the stock's April 4 closing price of $20.75.
DQE shareholders will receive the Allegheny Power dividend in effect at the time of the merger. Allegheny Power currently pays an annual dividend of $1.72 a share.
Allegheny Energy will have $6.2 billion in equity and $4.4 billion in net debt and preferred stock.
DQE's net debt and preferred stock as of December 31 was $1.7 billion.

Alan Noia, president and chief executive officer of Allegheny Power, will be chairman and CEO of Allegheny Energy. David Marshal, president and CEO of DQE, will be president and chief operating officer of Allegheny Energy.
The board of Allegheny Energy will have nine directors nominated by Allegheny Power and six by DQE.
Allegheny Energy will be based near Hargerstown, Md.
Allegheny Power and DQE said they expect to make merger-related savings of about $1.0 billion over a 10-year period.
They said the merger is expected to result in rates that are lower than if the companies remained standing alone.
The merger is conditioned on approval by shareholders of both companies and by state and federal regulators. The companies said they hope to receive all necessary approvals within 12 to 18 months.
Commenting on the merger deal, Allegheny Power's Noia said the combination strategically positions Allegheny Energy as a major regional player in the increasingly competitive electric power market.
Marshall said the merger is a natural fit for both companies.

They said the merged entity will have two million customers in five states -- Maryland, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia and West Virginia -- and a generating capacity of more than 11,000 megawatts of electricity.
